title: Keep the render pool working while tasks wait for a licence seat

blocks.text: The video service renders previews with a library that has a floating licence of a few seats. Every render task takes a seat before it calls the library, and the task that finishes a render gives the seat back. Both kinds of task run on the same render `ForkJoinPool`. On a quiet day it works. On a busy day the pool freezes: every seat is taken, more renders are waiting for one, and the finishing tasks that would give seats back are queued behind them, never started.
`LicenceSeats` keeps the seats in a `Semaphore`. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/LicenceSeats.java`: `take()` takes one seat, waiting if none is free.

When you're done, a render task waiting for a seat no longer stops the rest of the pool's work, and a task that takes a seat really holds one, so the count of free seats stays right. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: a render task that asks for a seat while one is free gets it
a task that waits for a seat gets in when one is given back
on a pool of one thread, a task waiting for a seat does not stop the task that gives a seat back from running
taking a seat while seats are free leaves exactly one fewer free

origin.section: A Worker That Blocks Is Lost to the Pool, Unless It Blocks Through managedBlock()

concepts: A worker blocked in an ordinary wait is lost to the pool, so waiters can hold every worker while the task that would release them sits in the queue; managedBlock lets the pool add a spare worker.
